A.biggest_strength: The unifying color-coded formula (ack = seq + len + SYN + FIN) dynamically tied to the sequence ladder, segment inspector, TCB state variables (SND.NXT/RCV.NXT), and real Linux packet traces.
A.biggest_weakness: Cites an unreleased/fictional "Linux 7.1" in the explanatory verification notes instead of an existing kernel release.
factual_errors: Mentions running on "Linux 7.1", which is not an existing Linux kernel release (likely intended Linux 6.1 or similar).

B.biggest_strength: Allows students to freely input arbitrary custom ISNs and payload byte sizes with correct 32-bit integer wrapping.
B.biggest_weakness: Completely omits the mobile viewport meta tag, causing mobile devices to render the page as an unreadable, tiny zoomed-out stamp.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is significantly superior as an educational tool for a networking class. Its visual design, typography, and color-coded mnemonic formula (ack = seq + len + SYN + FIN) make the core mechanism of TCP sequence and acknowledgment arithmetic immediately understandable. Page A also adapts flawlessly to mobile viewports with an adaptive SVG layout, while Page B fails severely on mobile due to a missing viewport meta tag, rendering as a tiny zoomed-out page. Furthermore, Page A offers deeper technical insight by tracking internal TCB state variables (SND.NXT and RCV.NXT) and comparing textbook numbers against real tcpdump traces.
